title: Reproducing the lottery-ticket hypothesis on a safety classifier to test pruning-vs-robustness

original_idea.body:
# Reproducing the lottery-ticket hypothesis on a safety classifier to test pruning-vs-robustness

**Problem:** The lottery ticket hypothesis (a small subnetwork can train to full accuracy in isolation) has been replicated on MNIST/CIFAR vision nets. Whether winning tickets exist for a *safety-relevant classifier* and — the twist — whether the pruned winning ticket retains the same out-of-distribution / adversarial robustness as the dense net is rarely checked together.

**Direction:** Train a small classifier on a harmful-vs-benign text or image-moderation dataset, run iterative magnitude pruning to find a winning ticket, and reproduce the ticket-trains-to-full-accuracy result. Then add the twist: evaluate the winning ticket vs. the dense network on held-out distribution shift / simple adversarial perturbations, reporting whether sparsity costs robustness.

**Why it matters:** Pruning/distillation is increasingly used to ship cheaper safety filters. If winning tickets match accuracy but lose robustness, that is a safety-relevant gotcha for deploying compressed models. The study reproduces a well-known result and adds a robustness lens, all on small networks trainable on a single consumer GPU with public data.

**Relevant context:** Lottery Ticket Hypothesis: winning tickets found in small MNIST/CIFAR nets, train in isolation to full accuracy; 'Proving the Lottery Ticket Hypothesis' (arXiv:2002.00585). Common Methodologies (context): learning-theoretic analysis. Steering priority (context): safety-tooling robustness, no lab resources.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Vague impact: pruning-vs-robustness on a safety filter is mostly a general-ML question with only a loose, non-catastrophic safety link.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Iterative magnitude pruning + robustness eval on a small classifier; mostly accessible but pruning loops add some work.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused deliverable (winning ticket accuracy + robustness comparison) though two evaluation axes.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Externally doable but lottery-ticket pruning is well-trodden; safety framing adds modest value.

low_compute.reasoning: Small classifier with iterative pruning, single GPU.

novelty.reasoning: Lottery tickets are well-studied; the pruning-vs-robustness-on-safety-task combination may be partly open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Lottery tickets and pruning-robustness are studied; the safety-classifier combination is a thin but plausible gap.
